faq: What does agent memory actually store?
Short notes about facts it may need later, such as a customer's preferences or the status of a case. We decide the exact fields with you and exclude anything sensitive you do not want kept.
Can I see and edit what it remembers?
Yes. In the Premium package we add a simple viewer, and in other packages the memory lives in a sheet or database that you can open and edit directly.
Is customer data safe in the memory?
It is stored in your own accounts with the access limits you choose. We apply data retention rules, but you remain responsible for privacy laws that apply to your business and customers.
Will memory make the agent more accurate?
It helps with consistency, but a wrong fact in memory can repeat itself. That is why we add update and forget rules and test with examples where facts change.

desc:
AI agent memory and context set-up gives your agent the right facts at the right moment, from customer history to past decisions. Ecom Swift LLC designs what it remembers, builds the storage in your own tools, and tests that it recalls correctly.

## Why an agent without memory repeats itself

Language models do not remember anything between requests unless you give the information back to them. Without a memory design, an agent asks a customer for their order number twice, forgets the instruction you gave it an hour ago, or treats a regular client as a stranger. The work feels clumsy, and people stop trusting it.

Memory is also not simply "more is better". If you pass everything every time, the agent slows down, costs more and gets distracted by old details. The goal is to keep the right facts and drop the rest.

## What is agent memory and context?

Context is the information the agent can see while it works on a single step: the instructions, the conversation so far and any facts you supply. Memory is the stored information that can be brought back into that context later.

We separate memory into three kinds. Task memory lasts for one job. Long-term memory holds facts about a customer, a case or a project for weeks or months. Forbidden memory is the list of things the agent must never store, such as payment card details or private health information.

## How good memory improves results

An agent that remembers can pick up a case where it stopped, use a customer's earlier preferences, and avoid repeating questions. That saves time for your team and reduces the number of replies that miss the point.

Accuracy also improves because the agent works from stored facts instead of guessing. When a customer's plan, address or last issue is retrieved from your own record, the agent does not have to invent it. Clean memory therefore supports both speed and correctness.

## What a good memory layer includes

- A written memory plan stating what is kept, for how long and why.
- Short-term memory that carries details across the steps of one task.
- Context trimming, so long histories are summarized instead of overflowing.
- Long-term records for customers or cases, stored in your own sheet or database.
- Rules to update a fact when it changes and to remove it when it expires.
- A list of data that must never be stored, enforced before anything is saved.
- Search over past work, so the agent finds the relevant record, not every record.
- Separate memory per customer or team, so one person's data never appears in another's reply.
- A simple viewer for people to read, correct and delete what the agent holds.

## How we build it

We start with a short workshop on what your agent needs to know to do its job well. We map each fact to its source: your CRM, order data, a help desk or a spreadsheet. Then we decide which facts belong in task memory and which belong in long-term storage.

We build the storage in tools you already own, so you can open and edit the data without us. We add the rules for updating and forgetting, and we build the step where the agent looks up what it needs before it answers. Finally we test on multi-step examples, including cases designed to trip it up, such as two customers with similar names. Packages scale from short-term memory for one agent up to a full layer with search, privacy rules and a viewer.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Store facts, not whole conversations, whenever a short summary will do.
- Record where each remembered fact came from.
- Give people a way to see and fix what the agent has stored.
- Set a retention period for each kind of data.
- Test memory with similar-looking cases to catch mix-ups.

**Avoid:**
- Saving sensitive data because it might be useful later.
- Mixing different customers' details in one shared memory.
- Letting outdated facts stay after a customer changes their details.
- Passing the entire history on every request.
- Treating memory as a replacement for your system of record.

## Who this is for

This service suits a support team whose agent keeps asking customers to repeat themselves. It suits a consultant who wants an agent to recall project decisions across weeks. It also suits a business that needs strict privacy rules, where the agent must be able to forget a person on request.

## What we need from you

Tell us what the agent should know, and share a few real multi-step cases. Give us access to the data source and the agent as a collaborator, team member or developer user, wherever the platform supports it. We never ask for passwords, and the memory lives in your own database or sheet.
